question: In each fast co-pyrolysis run of coal and biomass, what N2 flow rate, sample mass and holding time in the hot zone were used?
trap: the 20 °C/min heating rate or the 300 s purge
rendered:
<document title="Effects of sodium on nitrogen evolution characteristics during the fast co-pyrolysis of coal and biomass">

=== page 1 ===
- Acid-washed and Na-loaded samples, including individual SD/LC and blended samples (blending ratios of 5% and 15%), were pyrolyzed in a vertical fixed-bed reactor at 500 °C and 800 °C. The evolution of volatile-N (measured as NH3 and HCN) and char-N functional groups was analyzed using an FTIR gas analyzer and employing X-ray photoelectron and Raman spectroscopies.

=== page 2 ===
- The reagents used for macauba oil extraction included Hexane (100%, Synth, Brazil) and Anhydrous Sodium Sulfate P.A. (99%, Neon, Brazil), both of which were used as received without any further treatment.

=== page 3 ===
- After collection, the fruits were cleaned, peeled, and subjected to drying in a forced-air oven (Solab, model SL-100, 15,000 W) at 50 °C for approximately 72 h to reduce moisture content.

=== page 4 ===
- The extraction system consisted of three 1 L round-bottom flasks connected to Soxhlet extractors and condensers. In each extraction unit, 125 mL of hexane was used as the solvent for approximately 17 g of macauba palm almond, resulting in a solvent-to-sample ratio of approximately 1:7.3 (m/v).

=== page 5 ===
- The extraction process was conducted for approximately 5 h at about 70 °C using heating mantles.

=== page 6 ===
- The results demonstrate that Na promotes the release of NH3 and HCN during the pyrolysis of SD at 500 °C but inhibits it at 800 °C, whereas for LC and all blended samples, Na suppresses the release of both species at both 500 °C and 800 °C.

=== page 7 ===
- The N2 flow rate was 3 L min^−1, the sample mass was approximately 0.5 g, and the holding time in the hot zone was 20 min.

The answer is: 3 L min^−1, approximately 0.5 g, 20 min.
